subject: Temporary P1/P2 SLA adjustment request — HelixAI maintenance
messages:
From: Leah Park <l.park@helixai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@helixai.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary P1/P2 SLA adjustment for HelixAI maintenance

Hi Karthik,

We have a planned infrastructure maintenance for HelixAI the weekend of Mar 19–20 that will impact our ability to respond to incidents originating from our VPC (background DB maintenance + network patching). We expect a higher-than-normal incident rate during the 04:00–10:00 UTC window on both days.

We wanted to request a temporary SLA exception for P2 response time (allowing P2s to be handled within 3 hours during the maintenance window) and an agreed escalation path for any P1s. Specifically: 
- Confirm Redwood can accept a P2 temporary response window for the two maintenance days.
- Confirm who will be the primary on-call contact for P1 escalation during that time (Helix ops will own first triage; Redwood to provide on-call for escalations).
- Any required paperwork/approval (we can sign an addendum if needed).

Would appreciate a quick yes/no and proposed escalation contacts by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Leah
Leah Park
Director of Engineering, HelixAI
l.park@helixai.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: maintenance-window-times.csv (times with affected services)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <l.park@helixai.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P1/P2 SLA adjustment for HelixAI maintenance

Hi Leah — thanks for the heads up and the CSV with window times. We're able to accommodate a temporary P2 response window during the two maintenance days, subject to the following operational controls: 

1) Redwood will treat any P1 as high priority and follow our standard P1 response cadence (paged immediately, 60-min ack target).
2) For P2s during the maintenance window we can accept up to a 3-hour response window, provided HelixAI documents expected noise (approx. counts) and confirms a primary Helix ops contact for initial triage.
3) We require an internal playbook that defines: how Helix triages noisy alerts, the threshold to escalate to Redwood, and whether any alerts can be suppressed or routed to a delayed queue.

I'm looping in Priyom (support ops) to propose an on-call and escalation playbook. Marissa from Sales Ops is CC'd for contract/credit questions if this will affect billing. If you can share the expected alert counts by Friday EOD we can finalize the exception and ship an addendum.

Proposed next steps:
- Helix: share expected alert volumes (by service) — due Fri 12 Mar EOD
- Redwood (Priyom): propose temporary on-call handoff and escalation flow — due Mon 15 Mar
- Redwood (Karthik/Marissa): finalize addendum and any one-off credits — due Tue 16 Mar

Sound good?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the details, Leah. I pulled the CSV and sketched a temporary operational playbook — attached as SLA-exception-playbook-v1.pdf. High level: 

Summary of proposed operational controls:
- Coverage: Redwood will maintain an on-call responder in PST overlap hours (14:00–22:00 UTC) and provide a dedicated escalation contact outside that window via our on-call rotation.
- Paging: P1s -> immediate page to both Redwood primary on-call and Helix ops primary; P2s during maintenance -> routed to the delayed queue (3-hour response target).
- Triage thresholds: for noisy alerts we recommend Helix set a >=3 occurrences / 15m threshold before escalating to Redwood.
- Fallback: if Redwood on-call is unavailable, automatic failover to Redwood regional backup (SFO -> NYC) and then to an on-call manager (Priyom).

Operational notes: 
- We will run a joint dry-run on Thu Mar 18 (15:00 UTC) to test paging and escalation. Please confirm a Helix ops primary (name + mobile) to seed the playbook.
- We recommend standardizing alert tags for Helix services (service:helix-db, service:ingest, etc.) so our routing rules are accurate.

I've attached: SLA-exception-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook) and included a short runbook excerpt below.

--- runbook excerpt ---
1) Helix ops receives alert -> applies suppression rules -> if unresolvable after two suppress cycles escalate to Redwood by tagging alert with "redwood-escalate".
2) Redwood on-call ack target: 60 mins for P1, 3 hours for P2 (maintenance window only).
3) For any P1 that indicates customer-visible outage, Redwood will open a joint bridge and notify Karthik + Helix execs.

Attachments: sla-exception-playbook-v1.pdf

Let me know the Helix primary and we'll schedule the dry-run.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Support Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
